text: Good-breeding, and good-nature, do incline us rather to raise and help people up to ourselves, than to mortify and depress them, and, in truth, our own private interest concurs in it, as it is making ourselves so many friends, instead of so many enemies.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XLIII, to his son, London, July 1, Old Style 1748
